name: Arab socialism
summary: Arab socialism treats socialism as a national, non-Marxist means to Arab renewal and unity: state ownership of key industry, land reform and social services, with private property kept within limits and class struggle rejected in favour of national solidarity. It is anti-imperialist, non-aligned, hostile to Zionism, secular-leaning while respecting Islam, and in power became strong-executive, one-party rule.
scope: The mid-20th-century mainstream as set out in Aflaq and Bitar's Ba'th (1947 constitution) and Nasser's Egyptian regime (1962 National Charter, Arab Socialist Union). It excludes Marxist-Leninist Arab communism, Islamic socialism proper, and later Saddam-era or Qaddafist variants except where noted.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1947 Ba'th program promised free public health care and education to all, and Nasser's welfare state extended both.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The program seeks fairer distribution and worker protection but sets no wage floor; inferred from its redistributive aims.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The program has the state run major industry and control foreign and domestic trade, treating socialism as a necessary means of development.

public-ownership.rationale: Article 4 puts utilities, natural resources, large industry and transport under direct state management; Nasser nationalized banks, insurers and heavy industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Just redistribution of wealth was a founding aim and Nasser's reforms hit the landed elite, though the sources stress ownership caps more than tax rates.

unions-good.rationale: Workers were given a guaranteed share of assembly seats and profit-sharing, but unions were folded into the state party, so support is for state-guided labor.

property-fundamental.rationale: Art. 9 protects property and inheritance as natural rights only within the limits of national interest, so it can be overridden.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The state controls trade, abolishes foreign concessions and takes over large undertakings, a stronger stance than regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Free health care, education and guaranteed employment are core program planks, so welfare cuts contradict the platform.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers are to share in management and profits, but ownership of major firms belongs to the state, not workers collectively.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from the security-minded one-party regimes that suppressed opposition.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the moralistic, Islam-inflected social outlook of Nasserism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The program condemns sectarian and racial fanaticism yet calls speech freedom sacred; adherents in power restricted speech by other means.

strong-leader.rationale: Nasserism became a strong-presidency regime, and Nasser demanded a single executive as a condition of the 1958 union.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology rests on a strong state directing the economy and unifying the Arab nation.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the centralizing state that monopolized force.

empower-police-military.rationale: A strong national army was one of Nasser's six principles and the program makes military service compulsory.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the conservative-leaning social morality of the movement.

decide-locally.rationale: The program aims at one centralized, unified Arab state and state-run economy, not local decision-making.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented position on penal policy; adherents' regimes were harsh with political prisoners but welfare-minded in principle.

traditional-family.rationale: Nasserism drew on Islam as part of society's fabric while expanding women's education and rights; family traditionalism was not stated directly.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the socially conservative, Islam-influenced outlook of mainstream Arab socialist regimes.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the socially conservative, Islam-respecting stance of Nasserism.

more-religion-public.rationale: Nasserism was largely secular and subordinated Al-Azhar, yet it treated religion as part of the national identity; adherents are split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial injustice in the Western sense is not addressed; the program only opposes racial fanaticism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed; the program asserts equality of the sexes without a theory of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ba'th ideology is a romantic, spiritual nationalism centred on Arab cultural renaissance.

gradual-change.rationale: Aflaq sought a revolutionary structural transformation (inqilab) of Arab society and Nasser's regime enacted rapid reforms by decree.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Arab unity stresses free Arab movement but not mass immigration from outside.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nasser championed non-alignment and sovereignty, and was hostile to Western-dominated bodies, though he used the UN diplomatically.

free-trade.rationale: The program places foreign and domestic trade under direct state control and bans foreign concessions.

nation-first.rationale: Interests of the Arab nation come first, but Nasserism also pursued internationalist non-alignment solidarity with the Third World.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-imperialism and wariness of Western intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders among Arab states were sought, but not globally; inferred as disagree with the literal global claim.

limit-growth.rationale: Socialism was framed as a means to high production and national development, so growth limits contradict the aim.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no position in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Development and industrialization were seen as the route to national renewal, but no general claim about technology is documented.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from developmentalist statism and Egypt's own nuclear programme interest.

revolution-justified.rationale: Aflaq's inqilab is a revolutionary transformation, and Nasser came to power by coup and styled it a revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Technocratic planning was favoured but alongside populist mobilization; no clear stance.

central-planning.rationale: Nasserist policy based the economy on economic planning with a large public sector, though it kept some private property.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets and private property were tolerated under state supervision and ownership limits, as a mixed economy.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land policy was ceilings and redistribution rather than a land tax; inferred from that.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance is declared a natural right within national interest, so heavy taxation is not stated either way.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare was tied to employment guarantees and public services rather than cash transfers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: State control of trade and the aim of national industrialization imply protection of domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nationalized key sectors and central planning put investment under state direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land reform capped holdings and distributed land to smaller cultivators while keeping private property alongside the public sector.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nasser rejected Marxism and the program keeps wages and property, with profit-sharing for workers.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nasser nationalized banks and insurers to put finance under state control.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Arab Socialist Union grouped peasants, workers and others in a single state-run structure, with profit-sharing and managerial participation.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nasser's Arab Socialist Union was the sole legal party; the Ba'th was itself a ruling vanguard party, though early Ba'th texts favored representative rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nasserism overthrew the monarchy and made ending feudalism and the rule of capital core goals.

democracy-best.rationale: Ba'th texts endorse representative constitutional rule but in practice parties sacrificed it; adherents are split.

direct-votes.rationale: Nasser aspired to eventual direct democracy per one account, but practice was plebiscitary referendums; position unclear.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers got reserved assembly seats within a single-party state, not councils as the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: The aim is a single Arab state; secession would contradict unity and the movement fought separatist breakups.

natural-rulers.rationale: Nasser's regime was egalitarian against feudal elites, though it favoured a guiding vanguard; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Ba'th and free officers took power via coups and armed struggle against colonial rule and Israel.

war-builds-character.rationale: Aflaq's romantic nationalism stresses struggle and sacrifice, but no clear statement on war's character-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: Nasserism was largely secular but drew inspiration from Islam and did not impose strict separation; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Nasser abolished sharia courts and neutralized Al-Azhar, though Islamic teachings were cited to justify limits on ownership.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state directly runs key sectors and a compulsory national army.

military-superiority.rationale: Building a strong national army was a core Nasserist principle against Israel and imperial powers.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by Arab language and history across religions; it opposes sectarian and racial fanaticism, so not narrowly ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Ba'th ideology rejects Western economic determinism, seeing socialism as the conviction of a whole society rather than one class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Aims at equal opportunity and a just redistribution of wealth rather than full equality of outcomes.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Ba'th calls colonialism a criminal act and Nasser nationalized foreign assets; reparations not stated directly.

civilizational-union.rationale: Art. 6 aims to gather all Arabs in a single independent state, and the 1958 UAR attempted that.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Socialism is defined as sharing the country's resources among citizens; the ethic is collective and national.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Strong communal and national ethic yet the program also declares individual freedoms sacred.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Egypt later adopted family planning, but pan-Arab nationalists often favour numbers.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrial development was the goal of socialist planning.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Development was desired but no position on disruptive acceleration.

restore-past-order.rationale: It aims at a forward-looking renaissance and overthrew feudal old order, though it invokes a past Arab glory.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nasserist socialism was described as pragmatic, not doctrinaire, borrowing from Yugoslav experience.

direct-action.rationale: The Ba'th contested elections and seized power through parties and army coups, not mass direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: No documented doctrine; Nasser's regime used authoritarian means for democratic stated aims.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Development and industrialization are central aims.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: It rejects Marxist utopianism and keeps a wage and planning economy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by sharing national resources and social services, but wages and property remain, not full need-based communism.

production-for-use.rationale: Aflaq saw socialism as a means to production serving the nation's needs, but profit was not abolished.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Ba'th rejects Marxist economic determinism and class analysis; it limited ownership by its exploitative factor but allowed private enterprise.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Ba'th and Nasser opposed communism and class dictatorship, favouring cross-class national unity.

collective-farming.rationale: Land reform created smallholders with ceilings, with cooperatives, rather than collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialism blames Western imperialism, but the Marxist theory of capitalism causing war isn't adopted.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state-socialist program has the state run the economy and fund services.

harm-principle.rationale: The program values freedoms as sacred but state limits them by national interest.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Property rights are conditioned by national interest and the nation's collective rights dominate.

conscription.rationale: Art. 8 of the 1947 constitution makes military service compulsory.

exit-over-voice.rationale: It favors a constitutional representative regime as the check on the executive.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is meant to serve as a social provider, controlling economy, not a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Ba'th socialism pairs liberty with social justice, free education and health and guaranteed employment.

media-academia-power.rationale: None of the Ba'th or Nasserist texts discuss universities or media as rival power centres; neutral by silence.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The program condemns racial fanaticism and treats Arabs as one nation by culture and language.

organic-representation.rationale: The ASU organized representation by class sectors but not families or communities.

total-state.rationale: The state directs the economy, but not every area of life; religion and family were left partly independent.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Ba'th's name means renaissance or resurrection and its core aim is Arab national rebirth after decline.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Union of all Arabs in one state implies extending beyond present borders, though framed as unification, not conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Opposed feudalism and aimed to end it.

bound-labor.rationale: Ending feudalism was a core Nasser goal and land reform freed tenants.

universal-morality.rationale: Aflaq's thought is spiritual and national, with no stated universalist moral epistemology.

single-common-good.rationale: Ba'th socialism rests on the conviction of a whole society, not one class, aiming at a national common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism was named as an enemy alongside imperialism and colonialism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Rejection of Zionism implies rejecting Jewish immigration claims; it supports the Palestinians' return instead.

revive-national-language.rationale: Arabic is the shared national language; the question of reviving a lapsed one is not applicable.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers were to share in wages and management under the 1947 program, though under state oversight.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Ba'th program calls for free public education available to all.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: State-led development spending was central; no documented fiscal rule.

economic-freedom.rationale: It treats political and economic freedom as shaped by state direction and social justice rather than economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: No source claims rulers' moral example should replace law; the programme is built on constitutional and state institutions, so this is a weak inference.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement is anti-colonial and demands Arab independence and unity.

force-without-un.rationale: Nasser fought Western and Israeli powers without UN cover, but the doctrine is unstated.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Aflaq's thought has a spiritual and romantic emphasis and Islam as an Arab spiritual driver.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The program guarantees employment to citizens; no conditionality documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Ba'th and Nasserism rejected class struggle and stressed national unity across classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage is the basis of the Ba'th's romantic nationalism.

dominated-front.rationale: Non-alignment and anti-imperial solidarity were central, Nasser co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers are organized within the national framework and Ba'th socialism subordinates class to nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The 1947 constitution gives Arab women full civic rights and the Ba'th called for sexual equality.

ban-interest.rationale: The 1947 program set out to outlaw usury.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The program condemns racial fanaticism and colonialism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: It rejects Marxist class analysis, though it viewed pre-revolution states as serving landed elites.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Natural resources to be state-run; oil nationalism was a goal, and expansion is inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The sources never discuss immigration into Arab states; the programme only opposes sectarian particularism, so no stance can be derived.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not an Arab socialist doctrine; the program is anti-sectarian and not conspiratorial.

proportional-representation.rationale: The program calls for representative government without electoral specifics.

national-mission.rationale: Aflaq's Arab Mission of unity, liberty and socialism is a message to spread within the Arab world and beyond.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not an official doctrine; some Arab leftists criticized male dominance but the Ba'th stressed legal equality.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: They denounced the old landed elites and rich merchants and the Ba'th rose against them.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No eugenic doctrine, and the program condemns racial fanaticism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The regimes themselves ran security states; accountability for past abuses was not a theme.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The program has the state running large sectors, trade and welfare.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The program condemns racial fanaticism and treats Arabs as one nation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The program grants equal civic rights to women and rejects racial and sectarian particularism.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialism was framed as a national and pan-Arab project, not dependent on world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Zionism was viewed as an extension of European colonialism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Nasser abolished separate sharia courts, a step toward uniform law, but personal status law remained religious; split.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The program stresses freedom of belief.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No Arab socialist doctrine on cattle.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Nasserism regulated religion but retained Islamic instruction as part of national culture; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Strong state defense against imperial hostility fits Nasserism, though the withering-away idea is not discussed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1947 program calls the executive responsible to the people under a representative regime, though practice differed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Neither the 1947 programme nor the Charter states an export-surplus goal; it prefers state control of trade, with no stance on balances.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; the program opposes sectarian fanaticism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Nasser banned other parties and the Ba'th also outlawed rivals once in power.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Contradicts armed anti-colonial struggle and coups.

separated-powers.rationale: Power concentrated in a strong presidency and a sole party in practice.

vanguard-party.rationale: Ba'th rejects class-based revolution and communist doctrine, though it was itself a leading party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social justice and equal opportunity for the less fortunate, with land reform against feudal elite, were core.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not covered in the sources; adherents' state-ownership leaning is offset by their smallholder property aims.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Under the single-party state labor was channelled through the state's structures with strikes limited.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The movement blames feudalism, imperialism and capital for poverty, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The program opposes sectarian divisions but embraces diverse Arab religions in one nation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The program favors representative constitutional offices.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The regimes ruled under emergency measures to suppress opposition.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The state controlled internal trade, and Nasser's regime subsidized food and fixed prices.

party-controls-media.rationale: Nasser nationalized the press under the Arab Socialist Union.

party-commands-army.rationale: Nasser's army-led regime blurred party and army, and a strong national army was central; unclear.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed in the sources, so the ideology is treated as silent on residence periods.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Neither primary nor secondary sources mention pay of representatives, though the worker-peasant quota hints at populism.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Ba'th has an organized, disciplined party structure with a National Command.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Union of Arab states into one state is the central aim, an analogue of pooling sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Nasserist presidency commanded the army and appointed ministers.

clerical-rule.rationale: Nasserism neutralized Al-Azhar and rejected clerical political power.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The movement is nationalist and calls for national solidarity in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The program calls artistic freedom sacred, while the regimes censored art; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Nasser held the presidency by referendum with no limit.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources describe an executive responsible to the people but never mention recall mechanisms, so this is left neutral.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Non-alignment and ending foreign bases were central aims.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Property is limited but not abolished; no such program.

people-in-arms.rationale: The program makes military service compulsory in a national army, not a militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Land reform aided peasants but the movement pursued industrial development.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Art. 6 seeks union of all Arabs divided by colonial borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The Ba'th was led by intellectuals and students.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Aflaq claims a special Arab spiritual mission, though no hierarchy of cultures is stated.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; regimes executed political opponents and the position is inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative outlook; women's education was promoted.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: School science curricula are not addressed; Nasserism was secular-leaning yet respectful of Islam, so adherents are split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the moralist social outlook and Islamic influence.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not addressed in the sources; Arab nationhood is defined by language and culture rather than blood descent, so left neutral.

minority-language-support.rationale: The program centers on Arabic as the national language and opposes particularism.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Nationalist community-centred ethos, not individualist nonconformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialism and nationalization of foreign capital; debt cancellation is inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Abolishing foreign concessions and Nasser's nationalizations show political independence linked to economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The constitution was adopted by party convention and Nasser's charter by an appointed congress; no source demands an elected constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Present-day Nasserists frame autocratic excesses as necessary for revolutionary policies.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Third World solidarity suggests support but rationale of aid duty is not stated.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Egypt's rivalry with Israel and independence stance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Nasser was confirmed by referendum and the program makes the executive answerable to the people.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Banks were nationalized and finance put under state direction.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Zionism was deemed an enemy; mainstream stance was non-recognition (before 1970s).

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Art. 9 limits property and inheritance by national interest, and Nasser cited Islam to limit ownership.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not a topic of the doctrine; opposed Soviet dependence while cooperating with the bloc.

collective-defense.rationale: Arab joint defence pacts were pursued, with unity of Syrian and Egyptian forces.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The Arab left saw Israel's occupation after 1967 as the core wrong to be reversed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nasser neutralized Al-Azhar, regulated endowments and abolished sharia courts.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state led the sole party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The union of Syria and Egypt and unity aims imply keeping states together by force if necessary; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nasser demanded total union, not federal; autonomy for regions was rejected.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rejected monarchy, a sacral ruler contradicts its republican and secular tendencies.

character-from-environment.rationale: Social-justice reform presumes circumstances shape people, though not stated directly.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The program says the executive is responsible to the people under constitutional rule.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Representative constitutional government, not mixed rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Nasser was honoured publicly as the leader of the Arab nation.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Rejects class struggle and party leaders restoring capitalism as ideas; Nasserism claims national unity.

land-redistribution.rationale: Ceilings on holdings fell from 200 to 100 feddans and land was redistributed to farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Palestinian rights were redefined as central for the Arab left; return is a demand.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The program claims all Arab lands for a single Arab state on the basis of shared nationality.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Nasserism was secular-leaning and abolished sharia courts; the program stresses freedom of belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: Women have full civic rights and the regimes were secular.

common-currency.rationale: Pan-Arab union implies common currency but it was not documented.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union of all Arabs, one language-family people, is the central aim.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The program opposes particularism within the Arab nation.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Zionism rejected; the Arab left sees the Palestinians' homeland struggle as central, not emigration; inferred for Jews low.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nasser rejected Marxist historical materialism and determinism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The state controls trade and large undertakings and abolishes foreign concessions.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state controls finance and industry and supports public sector.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Workers and peasants quotas existed, but gender quotas were not stated.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Non-alignment pursued trade with both blocs; self-sufficiency in an Arab bloc, not a colonial bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: Socialism as a necessary means to production; Nasserist moralism existed but incentives remained.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Free Officers, a small group, started the 1952 revolution; Ba'th used military coups.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Nasserism abolished monarchy and feudal privilege.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Aflaq framed socialism as sharing resources and cooperation for national development; competition as the engine of progress is not an Arab socialist theme.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Ba'thist and Nasserist doctrine rests on the Arab nation's unity of language, history and culture, so schooling centred on Arab history follows.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-imperialism is central: the 1947 programme abolishes foreign concessions and Nasserism defined itself against colonial rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Ba'th programme stresses national education and compulsory service to build Arab national consciousness, and Arab Socialist Union Egypt promoted national loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-conscious admissions were not an Arab issue; inferred indifference, with socialist redistribution pulling one way and national unity the other.

public-money-creation.rationale: Nasserism nationalized key sectors and planned the economy, so state control of credit fits; money creation itself was not addressed.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Aflaq rejected economic determinism and Marxist crisis theory, so a collapse of capitalism was not doctrine; inferred from that rejection.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Arab nationalism arose against Ottoman and European rule and has no empire of its own to restore; inferred disfavour.

delink-world-market.rationale: Economic independence, nationalization of foreign capital and import-led industrialization suggest sympathy for reducing dependence, though trade with the Soviet bloc continued.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Arab socialists were anti-imperialist but rejected class struggle for national solidarity, so adherents would not clearly endorse this Leninist thesis.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The programme limits private property and expects state-directed equality, so inferred strong opposition to a right to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Ba'thist and Nasserist states concentrated power in a strong executive and single party, and subordinated rights to national goals.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Ba'th programme treats Arab unity as a single nation divided by imperial partition, so borders drawn by colonial treaties carry no binding force.

elective-rulers.rationale: The 1947 programme calls for representative government; inferred, since in power Nasserist presidents were confirmed by plebiscite rather than hereditary.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on national unity and a sole party; a single dissenter vetoing a collective decision cuts against it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Adherents were themselves revolutionaries against monarchies, but the regimes crushed opposition; inferred as split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Nasserism concentrated power in a strong presidency and a sole party, with the assembly subordinate; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a modernising, welfare-minded outlook that animal suffering is a mild moral concern.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that a development-minded movement accepts animal use for food and research with limited humane limits.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: Arab socialism puts social provision in the state and attacks privileged classes rather than relying on their charity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nasserism and the Ba'th demanded mass mobilisation behind national renewal, so withdrawal from politics is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; the regimes controlled mass media themselves for mobilisation, and the critique is a Marxist one the movement did not adopt.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; Arab socialism rejects Marxist class analysis, but its own regimes combined culture and coercion; inferred as split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-imperialism and the nationalisation of foreign capital rest on the view that foreign powers drained Arab wealth.

native-born-offices.rationale: The 1947 programme defines citizenship by Arab nationality across the Arab homeland, so reserving offices for natives of one state is inferred to be rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: Nasserism claimed a distinct Arab road to socialism, rejecting Marxism-Leninism and direction from Moscow.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from nationalisation of foreign capital and non-alignment, tempered by Nasser's acceptance of Soviet aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Arab socialism's nationalism treats Palestine as lost Arab land and Zionism as the enemy, and demanded its return.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; Arab nationalism treats Arabs as one people, so the settler-indigenous framing does not map and adherents would split.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as indifferent, as the movement's concern was imperialism and Zionism, not European fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Ba'th rejected communism but also moved against Western-style parties; inferred that adherents did not accept the equivalence thesis.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; a US historical question outside the movement's concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism: the Nasser regime removed monarchical and colonial symbols rather than preserving them.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a modernising state-feminism focus on women's civic rights (s1) and little engagement with men's-issues campaigns.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the same focus on women's civic rights and a conservative-leaning family culture.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Nasserism and the Ba'th held that Arab civilisation should develop its own political forms, not copy Western parliamentary models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Nasserism arose from the Free Officers' coup and treated the army as the vanguard guardian of the revolution.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; the 1947 programme promises women civic equality, but wages for domestic work is a later issue, inferred as split.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the Ba'th's respect for Arab-Islamic tradition and family; not a documented plank.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed as doctrine; Nasser's regime expanded merit-based civil service and graduate employment, but one-party patronage also shaped appointment.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nasser nationalised the Suez Canal Company and foreign firms, and Arab socialism put key industry under state ownership as anti-imperialist policy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; secular-leaning regimes liberalised some family law while respecting Islamic norms, so adherents are split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from the one-party, strong-executive practice of the Arab Socialist Union and Ba'th, which did not allow constituents to bind or remove leaders.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Arab socialism favoured state-run social insurance and public social services, and rejected private market provision for essentials.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land reform redistributed land to peasants and capped holdings, but kept private ownership within limits rather than making land communal and conditional on use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the strong executive and one-party rule in power, where assemblies had little real control over spending.

single-official-language.rationale: Arabic as the language of the nation is central to the Ba'th's Arab unity, with Arabisation of schooling and public life, though cultural minorities were often restricted.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist land and property nationalisations and Nasser's hostility to foreign holdings; not stated as a general rule.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the Arab socialist frame; class, not race, was the lens, and no group outcome standard was adopted.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the austere, anti-capitalist and national-solidarity ethos; consumer abundance was not a goal but was not condemned in the sources.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nasser's Egypt backed the Algerian FLN, Yemeni republicans and other anti-colonial or anti-monarchist movements, as Arab socialist policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from Nasser's Yemen intervention and Arab-unity ideal, which allowed pressing for unity or ideology across Arab states, though not an explicit doctrine.

corporate-influence.rationale: The movement fought private capital and foreign concessions in favour of state control of key industry; corporate lobbying is not discussed, so this is inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The Ba'th constitution abolishes foreign concessions and the movement was strongly anti-imperialist; foreign funding of civil society was not addressed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy was not a defining issue and Arab socialist states varied between promoting growth and family planning.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land ceilings and nationalisation limited ownership, but restricting property to local residents was not part of the programme.

job-guarantee.rationale: Nasserist planning and state employment of graduates imply a public duty to provide work; a formal guarantee is inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement saw Western democracies as imperial powers and favoured one-party rule, so it would doubt that spreading democracy brings peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The one-party Arab Socialist Union and strong executive imply a duty to obey the state; the point was not stated.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialism and non-alignment imply opposition to outside interference, although the regimes themselves intervened in other Arab states.

industrial-unions.rationale: Nasserist labour was organised through state-sponsored unions under the Arab Socialist Union; industry-wide structure is inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream Arab socialism blamed imperialism and Zionism rather than minorities within the nation, and Ba'th founders included Christians.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Ba'th constitution kept the family as a basis of society and respected religion; abolishing legal marriage is inferred as opposed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Single-party rule with a strong executive implies official secrecy; access to information was not addressed.

local-production.rationale: Nasserist import substitution favoured national self-sufficiency, but local production close to consumers was not a theme.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement relied on a vanguard party and the Arab Socialist Union as the sole organisation, the opposite of small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sovereignty and abolition of foreign concessions imply national law over foreign claims; international courts were not addressed.

religious-nation.rationale: The Ba'th defined the Arab nation by language, history and culture and was secular-leaning though respectful of Islam.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Arab socialism is anti-imperialist and non-aligned, calling for positive neutrality and equality between states rather than submission to a power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Central planning and Arab unity point to pooling national revenue rather than regional retention; this is inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The 1947 Ba'th constitution and Nasser's programme keep personal property and limited private ownership while placing key industry and utilities under the state.

defeat-communism.rationale: Aflaq rejected communism as a doctrine and Nasser suppressed communists at home, yet both states worked with the Soviet bloc and held to non-alignment.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: State ownership of utilities and key services is favoured; private provision within public funding is inferred to be disfavoured.

religion-illusion.rationale: Nasserism and the Ba'th are secular-leaning but respect Islam and reject the Marxist view that religion is an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Aflaq rejected economic determinism and Nasser rejected historical materialism, and both denounced capitalism as exploitative.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1947 programme gave women civic rights, but linking equality to transforming the economy is not documented; adherents are inferred to be split.

socialized-care.rationale: State social services were expanded, but public childcare and housework provision was not a programme goal; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Arabic and Arab culture are central to Arab nationalism, so protecting the language is inferred, though purge policy was not a core aim.

treaties-binding.rationale: Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal Company and foreign concessions regardless of earlier agreements, so binding treaties are inferred to be negotiable.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Arab socialism was state-led, with cooperatives only under state direction, not self-governing communities with common property; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Later Ba'thist governments, as in Iraq, settled Arabs in minority regions; this is inferred as a feature of the nationalist strand, not core doctrine.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Arab socialism presents itself as a national, non-Marxist socialism, a path between Western capitalism and Soviet communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Arab unity and the claim to Palestine rest on a shared homeland and history; no source states a general principle, so this is inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; inferred from mainstream Ba'thist and Nasserist doctrine, which fought Zionism politically rather than denying the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the doctrine; inferred from the conservative social norms of the regimes that applied it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Nasser's Egypt made the Arab Socialist Union the sole legal party and Ba'thist regimes also became one-party states.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The regimes were secular-leaning while respecting Islam; no stated position on punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The 1947 Ba'th constitution abolishes foreign concessions and the movement is anti-imperialist.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was secular-leaning and treated resistance as national rather than religious duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Nasser's state was secular but Islamic in character and fought the Muslim Brotherhood; inferred, not stated.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The doctrine favours strong-executive, one-party rule over direct popular participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Rejects class struggle and stresses national solidarity; the sources do not address overlapping oppressions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the socially conservative character of the regimes.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and no adherent consensus.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Aflaq rejected class struggle for national solidarity, which treats the left-right divide as secondary; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Aflaq rejected economic determinism and Marxist theory, so the alienation thesis is not part of the doctrine.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement respects Islam as part of Arab heritage and is hostile to the West mainly as imperialism; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The regimes were secular-leaning and grounded authority in the nation and the revolution; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; secular-leaning regimes but no stated rule on religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The 1947 constitution grants women civic rights, which suggests support, though workplace law is not addressed.

social-market-economy.rationale: The doctrine keeps private property within limits alongside state ownership of key industry, so it is neither laissez-faire nor fully state-run.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The 1947 constitution makes military service compulsory, and the regimes built large armies.

rich-first.rationale: Land reform, property limits and nationalisation aim to spread wealth rather than let some get rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Positive neutrality and non-alignment are in the 1947 programme, and Nasser co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Nasser's regime abolished the monarchy and the Ba'th constitution called for representative government.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Ba'th program put banking and key industry under state control, so state credit is favoured over user-owned mutual banks; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-imperialism and economic independence are core, so rejecting foreign lenders' conditions is inferred; the IMF era is later.

property-franchise.rationale: The Ba'th constitution calls for representative government and Nasser's charter set worker and peasant quotas, opposing wealth qualifications.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The Ba'th granted women civic rights but did not frame it with nature; not addressed.

reification.rationale: Aflaq rejected Marxist economic determinism, so this Marxist concept is not part of the doctrine; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Socialist limits on wealth suggest the critique would appeal, though regimes themselves controlled the press; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Nasserist and Ba'thist rule became strong-executive one-party rule using decrees and emergency powers.

racial-franchise.rationale: Arab nationalism defines the nation by language and culture rather than race, but one-party rule limited participation; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic to mid-20th-century doctrine; not addressed.

open-government-data.rationale: One-party systems kept decision records closed; inferred from the Arab Socialist Union's monopoly.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement is secular-leaning and stressed national unity across faiths; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Pan-Arab unity was meant to include Arab Christians and others, so singling out a religious minority contradicts it; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Aflaq and Nasser relied on a vanguard party and mass organizations like the Arab Socialist Union rather than lot-selected bodies; inferred from that structure, not stated.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Aflaq presented Islam as a cultural heritage of the Arab nation and Nasser's state brought religious institutions under modernizing control; inferred, as the sources do not discuss reinterpretation of doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Arab socialism aimed to curb the great landowners and capitalists, as in Nasser's nationalisations and land reform, and the 1947 Ba'th programme stressed social justice.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Ba'thist and Nasserist regimes were socially conservative and did not support open LGBT service; inferred from their regimes and nationalist-moral outlook.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Regimes were secular-leaning but kept Islam as state religion and Nasser did not promote atheism; Ba'th stressed a moral Arab heritage.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The regimes built strong security services and police states, so abolition is contrary to their practice and doctrine.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Arab nationalist unity doctrine favours a unitary state, and Ba'th and Nasserist rule were centralised and hostile to sectarian power-sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The strand holds that the state must provide welfare, health and education, as the Ba'th programme and Nasser's welfare state did.

term-limits.rationale: Nasser and Ba'thist leaders ruled for long periods under one-party systems and Nasser held the presidency until death, so limits are against practice.

vote-delegation.rationale: Single-party and mass-organisation rule via the Arab Socialist Union does not fit a liquid-democracy ideal.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: An anachronistic question for mid-century Arab socialism; no inferable stance.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Regimes were socially conservative on religious office and the Ba'th did not challenge male-only clergy, though they promoted women's education; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ba'th and Nasser promoted women's legal equality, education and work, but family law stayed traditional; inferred and mixed.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: Arab socialism stressed Arab national belonging and treated citizenship as tied to the Arab nation, so votes for foreigners were not a concern; a mild no.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: state-led social services and the Nasser-era rent reductions in Egypt fit a regime limiting private property for social welfare.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; the movement concerned state ownership of industry, not intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Ba'th and Nasserist regimes ran party youth organisations in uniform, such as the Ba'th Vanguards and Egyptian youth groups, to mobilise youth for the nation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the founding texts; regimes did seek weapons capabilities but also non-alignment.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-imperialism and positive neutrality were central: the movement rejected foreign bases, and Nasser campaigned against Western military pacts and bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; Arab socialism was more concerned with Israel and imperialism than with genocide recognition, and regimes' own records differ.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Arab socialism aimed at a socialist order where income comes from work, with limits on unearned private property and land reform ending rentier landlords.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Regimes were militarised one-party states that embraced armed struggle and national defence; the doctrine never held to nonviolence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Ba'th constitution holds the Arab nation to be an eternal one with a permanent mission, stressing continuity of Arab identity from ancient origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic to the movement.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: Arab socialism's unitary national project and conservative social policy make a postmodern critique of the category 'women' alien, though it promoted women's equality in law.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Ba'th and Nasserist regimes honoured shahid martyrs for the Arab cause and the nation as part of official political culture.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement was secular-leaning and framed politics through national and class interests; the Ba'th's founder Aflaq did give Islam a spiritual role, so a mild no.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the pan-Arab aim of unity gathers the people rather than keeping a diaspora; the Ba'th called for a single Arab state.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Ba'th sought the Arab renaissance through political union and state-building, with the party as the vehicle; cultural revival was not placed first.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the secular-leaning movement gave no view on gendered terms for God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; adherents showed no stance on feminist reading of religion.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: nationalisation of foreign and minority-owned firms, as in Egypt's 1956-61 measures, shifted the economy into national hands, though the primary aim was public ownership.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-Arab unity was the movement's core goal: the Arab nation should be one state, merging separate Arab states and regions.

independent-unions.rationale: Under the Arab Socialist Union the single party organised workers and peasants, so unions were party-aligned rather than independent.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The National Charter reserved half of ASU seats for workers and peasants, though real power stayed with the executive.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The 1947 constitution put public utilities under state control, and Nasser's nationalizations did the same.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the strong-executive, one-party model; the sources describe no second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: The programme favoured state ownership of key industry and limited private property, not ownership by local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the centralised planning state, which left no role for confederal assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the programme's aim of social justice and a fair distribution of income.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The ideology never addressed drug regulation and nothing in its principles settles it.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The ideology never addressed ageing research; no principle points either way.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the one-party state's tight control of finance and information.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the one-party regime's control of political expression and the press.

person-over-state.rationale: Aflaq subordinated the individual to the Arab nation and its renewal, and the regime ruled on that basis.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Aflaq held that Arab renewal has a spiritual side and the regime respected Islam alongside material development.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the centralised state, where local and regional bodies held delegated powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; Nasserist modernisation of agriculture points one way and nationalist self-sufficiency the other.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no principle of the ideology bears on urban density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Arab nationalism rests on language, history and culture rather than race, and stresses unity across groups.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Arab ancestry and heritage is central to Aflaq's nationalism, though it is framed as culture, not race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The ideology treated Zionism as an enemy and pursued Palestine's liberation, so it did not limit force to defence of the home territory.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Ba'th ideology holds the Arab nation is defined by shared language and history and should be one state despite colonial borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Ba'th and Nasser's regime were secular-leaning and sought national unity over sectarian divisions, so rejected separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Arab socialism is anti-imperialist and treats the colonial division of the Arab lands and Zionism as Western projects to weaken the Arabs.

free-public-college.rationale: The 1947 Ba'th program and Nasser's welfare state provided free education to all, including university.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Mid-century Arab socialism focused on industrialisation and never addressed pollution taxes; nothing in the sources points either way.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national renewal and development for coming generations; not stated in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The regimes promoted women's education and work, but the sources do not describe a distinct-values claim.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the regimes' large militaries and rearmament as part of anti-imperial struggle.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of colonial-era secret treaties such as Sykes-Picot and the stress on non-alignment.

capital-controls.rationale: Nasser nationalised banks and foreign capital in 1961 and the state directed the economy; controls on capital movement fit this.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the strong-executive, one-party regimes the movement produced, which centralised armed force in the state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the movement was nationalist and army-led (the Free Officers), and prized military strength for Arab renewal, so refusing orders is unlikely to be endorsed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Never addressed directly; under the Arab Socialist Union unions were folded into a state-run corporatist structure, so adherents are split between worker rights and state control.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: the programme relied on state ownership, land reform and social services rather than topping up market wages.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: state-planned development and public spending were central, and no fixed borrowing limits appear in the programme.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The movement was anti-imperialist and non-aligned, abolished foreign concessions and sought a fairer position for Arab and developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Nasser's regime and the Ba'th took over and used the existing state through army-led seizures of power, rather than dismantling it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: It set out a state-led socialist blueprint with public ownership of key industry and limits on private property, not open economic pluralism.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: ecological accounting was unknown to the movement, whose socialism centred on state ownership of resources for national development.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Arab nation is treated as an eternal community with a lasting mission, though the Ba'th framing is secular-leaning rather than strictly religious.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Never addressed; the regimes offered free education, so student loans were not an issue, and the answer is inferred as neutral.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: national solidarity and unity were stressed over regional or class grievances inside the Arab state.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Aflaq's spiritual, humanist framing of Arab renewal, which assumes common human values.

public-service-media.rationale: Nasser's regime nationalised the press and ran broadcasting as a state tool, so independent public media were not part of the model.

missingStatements.text: Socialism should be a means of national development and unity rather than a doctrine of class struggle.
missingStatements.rationale: Aflaq defined socialism as a necessary means to production and national renewal, and Nasser rejected class struggle and historical materialism.

missingStatements.text: Foreign companies and concessions in the country should be abolished or taken into public ownership.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1947 constitution abolishes foreign companies and concessions, and Nasser nationalized foreign capital in 1961.

missingStatements.text: A fixed share of legislative seats should be reserved for workers and peasants.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1962 National Charter guaranteed workers and peasants at least half of assembly seats.
missingStatements.declined: Specific institutional device of one constitution; too narrow for the bank.

missingStatements.text: Countries should stay out of both Cold War blocs and pursue positive neutrality.
missingStatements.rationale: Non-alignment is in the 1947 programme and Nasser co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement.

notes: The Ba'th (parliamentary rhetoric, pan-Arab party) and Nasserism (sole-party presidency) differ on democracy, and later Ba'thist regimes moved further to personalist authoritarianism; answers use the shared core and the Nasser-era peak. Many social questions (drugs, abortion, LGBT, family) were not addressed and are low-confidence inferences.
